relations.note: Both turn real scenes into interactive simulation for manipulation learning. This is a retrospective topical connection: RialTo predates SimFoundry and does not cite it. SimFoundry expands automation and scene diversity.

Both combine few real demonstrations, simulation RL, and a visual student for deployment. ExoStart uses an exoskeleton and dynamics filtering; RialTo uses visual-policy rollouts in a scene twin. This is not a citation claim.

ai_summary.one_liner: RialTo uses reconstructed deployment scenes to turn demonstration-trained manipulation into disturbance-tolerant behavior through simulation RL.
ai_summary.problem: A small behavior-cloning dataset rarely covers recovery from unexpected object motion or clutter.
ai_summary.solution: Reconstruct the scene, obtain successful simulator trajectories with privileged states, train a state policy with demonstration-augmented PPO, and distill to point-cloud observations while retaining real demonstrations.
ai_summary.key_result: Section IV-A reports 91/77/75% success for pose randomization/distractors/disturbances versus BC at 25/11/5%. The main comparison uses 15 simulator demos plus 15 real demos for co-training; the real-only initialization route is tested separately.
limitations: Depth-sensor failures on thin, transparent, or reflective objects.
Evidence focuses on rigid and articulated objects in relatively quasistatic tasks.
Approximately two days of end-to-end training per task.
Best-policy evaluation and at least ten real rollouts per condition leave deployment reliability uncertain.

research_gaps.question: How can the policy support thin, reflective, and transparent objects when depth reconstruction is unreliable?
Can the pipeline handle deformable objects and faster interactions that require accurate physical parameters?
How can end-to-end task learning be reduced from about two days to a practical continual-adaptation cycle?
Do robustness gains persist under seed-averaged evaluation, many more trials, and genuinely unseen deployment scenes?

future_directions: Investigate RGB or RGB-D students to reduce dependence on reliable depth alone.
Extend interactive reconstruction and simulation to deformables and identify physical parameters for dynamic tasks.
Accelerate point-cloud learning and parallelization to shorten the adaptation loop.
Evaluate many seeds and repeated hardware trials before extrapolating to unattended deployment.
evidence_notes: Latest arXiv v3 is authoritative for results; the project abstract retains the earlier six-task wording.
Figure 5 covers six core tasks; the paper describes eight tasks overall including in-the-wild additions.
Section IV-A rounded averages are quoted as reported; Figure 5 labels are individually rounded.
Table III reports simulation results and is not a real-world success table.
Public captions are original explanatory paraphrases; source figure/table numbering is retained.
